integrity.finite_replay: The standalone verify.py passed 3013 checks including all labeled trees through eight vertices.
integrity.principal_evidence: Rooted-forest bijection and specified-leaf deletion; exact finite difference; uniform distance-scale Taylor and Rayleigh-tail arguments.
integrity.priority_comparison: The s=0 off-path subcase is covered via Joyal mapping; only endpoint/off-path coupling and its nonmonotone optimized consequence are claimed distinct.
integrity.publication_claim: No publication or independent certification claimed.
integrity.source_date_basis: University of California Berkeley report 457 publicly dated September 1, 1996; accessible full-text copy is marked revised in 1998.

limitations: Uniform labeled Cayley trees with two distinct fixed marked vertices, not arbitrary random-tree models.
For fixed conditional distances the Rayleigh-scale correction in the limiting regression requires a different constant; stated limit assumes distance tends to infinity.
Older multivariate tree enumerators may implicitly imply the conditional generating polynomial despite targeted negative searches.
Computations only verify finite cases; general formulas rely on the written proof.

The off-path-only factorial moments and leading distance covariance have equivalents in uniform random mapping statistics through the classical Joyal correspondence; novelty is confined to the coupled marked-endpoint law and cubic-root optimum.
title: A path-conditioned leaf law and its cubic-root optimum in uniform labeled trees
